item.title: Dunwei Wang Named Interim Director of the Schiller Institute
item.description: Dunwei Wang has been named the interim Seidner Family Executive Director of the Schiller Institute for Integrated Science and Society.

item.title: Katherine McNeill Receives $2 Million Grant to Redesign Science Curricula
item.description: With the help of a $2 million grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF), Katherine McNeill is redesigning science curricula to make learning science more equitable and accessible for Boston Public School students.

item.title: BC Falls to NC State Despite Setting Shooting Record, Loses 15th Straight Game
item.description: Boston College women's basketball set a program record with 16 made three-pointers, but it was not enough to slow down a potent NC State offense as the Eagles fell 106–84.

item.title: ‘Wonder Man’ Lacks the Wonder of a Typical Marvel Project
item.description: The quality of productions from Marvel Studios has been wildly inconsistent after the ground-breaking success of Avengers: Endgame. Unfortunately for fans, Marvel’s latest TV show falls on the negative end of that spectrum.

item.title: Newton Joins Amicus Brief Blocking Trump’s Mass Deportation Drive in Minnesota
item.description: The City of Newton signed on to an amicus curiae brief urging that President Donald Trump’s Operation Metro Surge, the initiative aimed at deporting undocumented immigrants in Minnesota’s Twin Cities, violates the Constitution.

item.title: Newton Zoning Board of Appeals Discusses Updates to Controversial Proposed Development in Nonantum
item.description: The Newton Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) met on Wednesday to discuss changes made to a proposal for a Nonantum development, prompting significant criticism from the public and board members about the project's overall impact on the local community.

item.title: West Newton Cinema Honors International Holocaust Remembrance Day
item.description: In the wake of International Holocaust Remembrance Day this past Tuesday, families took their seats at West Newton Cinema for the screening of Among Neighbors, followed by an exclusive recorded question-and-answer session featuring the film’s award-winning director, Yoav Potash.

item.title: No. 13 BC Plays Spoiler in 4–1 Win at BU as Offense Rides Into Beanpot Hot
item.description: No. 13 BC men's hockey beat BU 4-1 on the road on Friday night, sending the Eagles into Monday's Beanpot Semifinal on a three-game win streak.

item.title: Black Bears Fend Off Late Surge, Top BC 4–3
item.description: BC women's hockey suffered its ninth loss in 11 games as Hockey East foe Maine scored three third-period goals and beat the Eagles 4–3 on Friday night.

item.title: BC Falls Off Late in 73–66 Home Loss to No. 17 Virginia
item.description: BC men’s basketball (9–12, 2–6 Atlantic Coast) delivered a nail-biter, but No. 17 Virginia (18–3, 7–2) ultimately came out on top 73–66 as simple mistakes plagued the Eagles in big ways.
